answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a wharf of chained task receipts: every completed job leaves a receipt signed by the counterparty and linked to the one before it. Trust grows only as real counterparties add links, so a newcomer starts empty. A jade token minted from thin air buys nothing, because a copied receipt breaks the chain hash, and spinning up a hundred fresh identities means doing a hundred separate chains of genuine work, since no receipt can be reused across identities. The anchor is the work itself: cheap to verify, expensive to fake at scale.
